{"draft": "Vici Properties Q3 2026: AFFO Growth Despite CECL Hit
Vici Properties delivered higher AFFO per share in the third quarter as revenue climbed, even as a CECL allowance change weighed heavily on reported earnings.
Total revenues reached $1.1 billion, up 5.8% year-over-year. The result included $132.0 million of non-cash leasing and financing adjustments and $19.0 million of other income, pointing to continued flow-through from the portfolio.
Net income attributable to common stockholders slipped 55.1% to $342.5 million, or $0.31 per share, with the decline driven by the $478.2 million aggregate change in the CECL allowance. AFFO attributable to common stockholders fared better, growing 7.5% to $685.2 million, while AFFO per share rose 4.3% to $0.62.
On capital, the company issued $1.75 billion of investment grade senior notes at an adjusted weighted average interest rate of 5.422% to refinance 2026 maturities. It ended the quarter with $270.3 million in cash and cash equivalents, approximately $17.2 billion in total debt and approximately $2.5 billion in liquidity. The quarterly cash dividend was declared at $0.46 per share, up 2.2% year-over-year, and, subsequent to quarter-end, the board authorized a share repurchase program for up to $2.0 billion.
Outlook: Vici Properties raised AFFO guidance for full year 2026 to between $2,695 million and $2,705 million, or between $2.47 and $2.48 per diluted share."}
